stem.en:
Madina's class keeps two goldfish in a tank by the window. Each week a different pair of students feeds them, and a chart on the classroom door shows the names for every week of the term. The fish get a small pinch of food in the morning and nothing in the afternoon.

According to the text, how do the students know whose week it is to feed the fish?

options.en: A chart on the classroom door lists the pair for each week.
The teacher chooses a new pair every morning before lessons.
The pair who fed them last week choose the next pair.
The names are written on a card beside the tank.

why.en: The text says 'a chart on the classroom door shows the names for every week of the term'. The tank is by the window, and no one picks pairs day by day.
why.uz: Matnda «a chart on the classroom door shows the names for every week of the term» deyilgan. Akvarium deraza yonida, juftlarni hech kim har kuni tanlamaydi.

The wind was too strong for the cabins.
Too few visitors had come to ride it.
Its cabins were being painted that day.

Every evening at six, the bakery near the bus station cuts the price of the bread that is left by half. Whatever is still unsold at closing time is not thrown away: the baker's son takes it to the old people's home at the end of the street, where it is toasted for breakfast the next morning.

According to the text, what happens to the bread that is still unsold when the bakery closes?

options.en: It goes to an old people's home and is toasted the next morning.
It is sold at half price the following morning.
It is thrown away so that the shelves are clear for the new bread.
The baker's son eats it with his own family for breakfast.

why.en: Unsold bread 'is not thrown away': the baker's son takes it to the old people's home, where it is toasted. Half price is at six in the evening, before closing.

According to the text, what must a resident do when borrowing a tool?

options.en: Write the date and the tool's name in the cupboard notebook
Ask the caretaker for the key to the tool cupboard on a Friday
Return the tool on the same day, before the room closes
Pay the mahalla a small fee for each day the tool is kept

why.en: A borrower 'writes the date and the tool's name in a notebook'. Tools may be kept up to three days, and the caretaker only checks the notebook on Fridays.
why.uz: Oluvchi daftarga sanani va asbob nomini yozadi. Asbobni uch kungacha olib turish mumkin, mahalla xodimi esa daftarni faqat juma kunlari tekshiradi.
why.ru: Тот, кто берёт инструмент, пишет в тетради дату и название. Держать его можно до трёх дней, а смотритель лишь проверяет тетрадь по пятницам.

stem.en:
Many people believe that a camel stores water in its hump. In fact, the hump is mostly fat. When food is scarce on a long desert journey, the camel's body slowly uses up this fat for energy, and the hump shrinks and may even lean to one side. Camels go without water for long periods for other reasons, such as losing very little water when they breathe.

According to the text, what happens to a camel's hump when food is scarce?

options.en: It shrinks as the camel's body uses up the fat inside it.
It fills with water that the camel saves for the dry days ahead.
It grows larger to protect the camel from the heat.
It stays the same size until the camel finds water.

why.en: The text says the body 'slowly uses up this fat for energy, and the hump shrinks'. The idea that the hump holds water is the belief the text corrects.
why.uz: Matnda tana «slowly uses up this fat for energy, and the hump shrinks» deyilgan. Oʻrkachda suv saqlanadi degan fikrni matn rad etadi.
why.ru: В тексте: организм «slowly uses up this fat for energy, and the hump shrinks». Мысль, что в горбу вода, текст как раз опровергает.

stem.en:
Salt is spread on icy roads because it lowers the temperature at which water freezes, so ice with salt on it melts even a little below zero. But in very hard frost the salt can no longer melt anything, and in the coldest weeks of winter the road crews in mountain districts switch to sand. Sand melts no ice at all; it simply gives tires something rough to grip.

According to the text, why do road crews in mountain districts use sand in the coldest weeks?

options.en: Salt stops melting ice in very hard frost, but sand still gives tires grip.
Sand melts ice faster than salt does when the frost is very hard.
In very hard frost, salt raises the temperature at which water freezes.
Sand is cheaper than salt and easier for the crews to spread.

options.en: In this family, a weaver proves herself by improving an old pattern, not by copying.
A good apprentice should copy every one of the master's patterns exactly.
Girls in the family learn weaving by copying patterns knot by knot.
The family no longer weaves any of the grandmother's old patterns.

why.ru: После «see it differently» копирование — лишь первый шаг: девушка становится ткачихой, когда улучшит старый узор.

For his first match as goalkeeper, Ravshan had borrowed his cousin's gloves, which were two sizes too big. The other team scored twice in the first ten minutes, and the boys on the bench laughed. At half-time Ravshan took the gloves off, laid them on the bench and played the second half bare-handed, and the ball did not get past him again.

Ravshan is a poor goalkeeper, and the boys on the bench are right to laugh.
Ravshan is angry with his cousin for lending him gloves that are too big.
Goalkeepers always play better without any gloves on their hands.

why.en: In gloves 'two sizes too big' he lets in two goals; without them, 'the ball did not get past him again': the poor start came from the gloves.
why.uz: «two sizes too big» qoʻlqopda u ikki gol oʻtkazib yuboradi; ularsiz «the ball did not get past him again»: yomon boshlanishga qoʻlqop sabab edi.

Spiders' webs are usually thought of simply as traps. Many spiders, though, use their silk in other ways as well. A young spider may let out a long thread and be carried by the wind to a new home; a mother may wrap her eggs in a thick silk case; and a spider dropping from a branch trails a line behind it, so that it can climb back up if it falls.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: Spiders use their silk for far more than catching their prey.
A spider's silk is used mainly to build the web that traps insects.
Young spiders travel to new homes on threads carried by the wind.
Spiders that wrap their eggs in silk do not build webs.

why.en: After 'though', the text lists travel on the wind, egg cases and safety lines: silk does much more than make traps. Travel on the wind is one example only.
why.uz: «though» soʻzidan keyin matn shamolda koʻchish, tuxum qopchigʻi va xavfsizlik ipini sanaydi: ipak tuzoqdan ancha koʻp ishga yaraydi.
why.ru: После «though» текст перечисляет полёт на ветру, кокон для яиц и страховочную нить: шёлк нужен не только для ловушек.

Their coach explained that his students had spent less time learning speeches by heart and more time listening to the other side, so that every answer they gave met the argument actually made rather than the one they had expected.

options.en: The younger team won by answering the arguments actually made, not prepared ones.
The oldest students win debating contests because they have the most practice.
Learning speeches by heart is the best way to prepare for a debate.
The eighth-grade team had practiced for longer than any other team.

why.en: The class expected the oldest to win; the eighth graders did, by listening and meeting 'the argument actually made': listening beat experience here.

why.ru: Класс ждал победы старших, а выиграли восьмиклассники: они слушали соперников и отвечали на «the argument actually made».

For years Malika had walked past the old woman who sold sunflower seeds at the bus stop without looking at her. One rainy morning, when the bus was late, the woman held her umbrella over Malika's head without a word. Since then, Malika has bought a paper cone of seeds every morning, though she does not much like sunflower seeds, and the two of them talk about the weather until the bus comes.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

Malika buys the seeds every morning because she has grown to love them.
The old woman sells more seeds on rainy mornings than on dry ones.
Malika is still unwilling to look at the woman at the bus stop.

why.en: She once walked past without looking; after the umbrella, she buys seeds daily though she 'does not much like' them, and they talk: the kindness changed things.

stem.en:
It is widely assumed that the best place to keep bread is the refrigerator, since cold keeps food fresh. Bread is an exception. In the cold, the starch in bread hardens faster than at room temperature, so a loaf kept in the refrigerator goes stale sooner, even though it grows mold more slowly. For bread that will be eaten within a few days, a cloth bag in a cool cupboard is better; for longer, the freezer.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: Though cold keeps most food fresh, the refrigerator makes bread go stale faster.
The refrigerator is the best place to keep every kind of food fresh.
Bread kept in the refrigerator grows mold more slowly than other bread.
Bread should always be kept in the freezer, however soon the family is going to eat it.

why.en: After 'Bread is an exception', the text says cold makes bread stale sooner. Slower mold is a detail it grants, and the freezer is only for bread kept longer.
why.uz: «Bread is an exception» soʻzlaridan keyin matn sovuqda non tezroq qotishini aytadi. Sekinroq mogʻorlash bir tafsilot, muzlatish kamerasi («freezer») esa uzoqroq saqlash uchun.
why.ru: После «Bread is an exception» текст говорит, что в холоде хлеб черствеет быстрее. То, что плесень появляется медленнее, — лишь деталь, а морозилка — для долгого хранения.

stem.en:
To most visitors, the narrow, winding lanes of the old town center look like the result of poor planning. The builders who laid them out may have known exactly what they were doing. In summer the tall walls on either side keep the lanes in shade for most of the day, and the turns break up the hot wind from the desert, so the lanes stay cooler than the wide, straight streets of the newer town.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: The lanes that look badly planned actually keep the old center cool.
The lanes of the old town center were laid out with no plan at all.
The newer town's wide streets are hotter because the walls along them are low.
Hot desert winds blow through the old town center all summer long.

why.en: After the visitors' view of poor planning, the text shows shade from tall walls and turns that break the hot wind: the lanes were laid out to stay cool.
why.uz: Mehmonlar fikridan keyin matn baland devorlar soyasi va issiq shamolni toʻsadigan burilishlarni koʻrsatadi: torkoʻchalar salqin boʻlishi uchun qurilgan.
why.ru: После мнения гостей о плохой планировке текст показывает тень высоких стен и повороты, гасящие горячий ветер: улочки проложены так, чтобы в них было прохладно.

Sherzod, who looks after his school's rabbit, claims that the rabbit eats more hay when the hay is put in a rack above the floor than when it is spread on the floor of the hutch.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Sherzod's claim?

options.en: The rabbit ate more hay on days when it was in the rack than on days when it lay on the floor.
Hay that is spread on the floor of the hutch gets trodden on and dirty far more quickly than hay kept in a rack.
The rabbit drinks more water in summer than it does in winter.
Sherzod fills the hay rack every morning before his lessons begin.

why.en: The claim compares the rack with the floor. Only the finding that the rabbit ate more on rack days compares the two; dirty hay is a possible reason, not a result.
why.uz: Daʼvo osma oxur bilan polni solishtiradi. Faqat oxur kunlari quyon koʻproq yegani haqidagi natija ikkalasini solishtiradi; iflos pichan esa natija emas.
why.ru: Утверждение сравнивает кормушку и пол. Сравнивает их только результат о том, что в дни с кормушкой кролик ел больше; грязное сено — лишь возможная причина, а не результат.

Asror thinks that his younger brother falls asleep faster on evenings when the family switches off the television an hour before bedtime than on evenings when it stays on.

His brother falls asleep fastest of all on evenings after a long afternoon of football practice with his friends.
The family usually watches the television together for an hour after dinner.
His brother's bedroom is at the far end of the flat from the television.

why.en: Asror's idea links the television being off to falling asleep faster. Only the finding that his brother fell asleep sooner on those evenings supports it.
why.uz: Asrorning fikri televizor oʻchirilishini tezroq uxlash bilan bogʻlaydi. Faqat ukasi oʻsha kechalari tezroq uxlagani haqidagi natija buni tasdiqlaydi.

Ozoda noticed that the students in her class who eat breakfast at the school canteen arrive on time for lessons more often than the others. She concluded that eating breakfast at school helps students arrive on time.

options.en: When the canteen was closed for a week, the students who usually ate there still arrived on time as often as before.
Students who eat breakfast at the canteen say that they feel more awake and ready to work in the first lesson of the day.
The canteen serves porridge, eggs and tea for breakfast every morning.
Most students in Ozoda's class live within walking distance of the school.

why.en: If the usual canteen eaters still came on time when the canteen was closed, breakfast at school is not what gets them there. That weakens the conclusion.

In a short story, the narrator describes her little cousin, Mohira, as the most curious child she has ever known.

"She was small for her age and always wore her hair in two long braids, each tied at the end with a bright red ribbon."
"She cried whenever anyone left the room, even if they were only going to fetch water."
"She could sit and draw for hours without saying a single word to anyone."

why.en: Curious means wanting to know things. Only the line in which she asks why bread rises, where the river goes and what is in every box shows that.
why.uz: Qiziquvchan — hamma narsani bilishni xohlash. Faqat non nega koʻtarilishi, daryo qayerga oqishi va qutilar ichini soʻragan satr buni koʻrsatadi.
why.ru: Любопытный — тот, кто хочет всё знать. Это показывает только строка, где она спрашивает, почему поднимается хлеб, куда течёт река и что в коробках.

A gardener who grows tomatoes behind her house claims that her tomato plants have had fewer insects on them since she began planting basil between some of the rows.

Basil grows quickly in the warm weeks of early summer.
Insects are most common on tomato plants in the hottest and driest weeks of the summer, in July and August.
Several of her neighbors have begun planting basil in their gardens too.

Many of the café's regular customers told the owner that the free internet was the main reason they had started coming in.
The café also serves sandwiches and fresh juice.
The owner pays a fixed fee for the internet each month.

In a poem about walking home late through her city, the speaker describes the empty streets. A student claims that the speaker presents the city at night as both lonely and comforting.

Which quotation from the poem most effectively illustrates the student's claim?

"The streets are empty under the lamps, / and the wind runs cold along the river wall."
"Each lit window glows like a lantern in the dark, / and the bakeries already smell of morning bread."
"At dawn the buses fill again with noise, / and the market stalls begin to open."

why.en: Lonely: 'The streets are empty'. Comforting: each lit window 'seems to keep me company'. Only this quotation shows both; another shows only the emptiness.

The history section is the quietest part of the library in the afternoon, when few students come in.
The cat sleeps for about three hours every afternoon.
Students rarely borrow books from the third shelf of the history section.

why.en: If the cat followed the pipe to the science shelves, the warmth of the pipe is what draws it. A quiet or undisturbed shelf points to other causes.

The makers of a new bicycle lock claim that it cannot be cut through with ordinary tools in less than ten minutes. They plan to sell it in sports shops across the country next year.

The new lock weighs more than most of the other locks sold in the same shops.
Most bicycles stolen in the city are taken in the evening, near shops and cafés.
Several riders in a cycling club said that they felt much safer leaving their bicycles outside with the new lock.

why.en: The claim is that ordinary tools need over ten minutes. An ordinary hand saw cutting it in four contradicts that directly; feeling safer is not a test of the lock.

why.ru: Утверждение: обычным инструментом нужно больше десяти минут. Обычная ножовка за четыре минуты прямо ему противоречит.

Most of the singers say that they enjoy the warm-up exercises and would like to keep doing them before every rehearsal.
The choir sings at four concerts every year.
The warm-ups were first suggested by a singer from the town theater.

stem.en:
After a school painted its classroom walls a pale green, fewer students were sent to the nurse with headaches. The head teacher concluded that the new color had reduced headaches.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the head teacher's conclusion?

options.en: The number of headache visits had begun to fall two months before the walls were painted.
Many students said that the pale green walls made their classrooms feel calmer and more pleasant to work in.
The painters finished all of the classrooms in a single week.
The school nurse now keeps a record of every visit and its cause.

why.en: If headaches were falling two months before the painting, the fall started without the new color. That weakens the head teacher's conclusion.
why.uz: Bosh ogʻriq devor boʻyalishidan ikki oy oldin kamaya boshlagan boʻlsa, pasayish yangi rang paydo boʻlmasdan oldin boshlangan. Bu xulosani zaiflashtiradi.
why.ru: Если головные боли пошли на убыль за два месяца до покраски, снижение началось без нового цвета. Это ослабляет вывод.

stem.en:
Zuhra noticed that the milk her family buys from a neighbor's cow tastes sweeter in summer than in winter. She thinks the difference comes from the fresh grass that the cow eats in summer.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Zuhra's idea?

options.en: In a summer when the cow ate only dry hay in the barn, its milk tasted the way it does in winter.
In winter the neighbor milks the cow later in the morning than in summer, after the sun has warmed the barn.
The neighbor sells the cow's milk in glass jars in every season.
Most families in the village prefer the taste of summer milk.

why.en: If summer milk tasted like winter milk once the cow ate only dry hay, the fresh grass is what makes the difference. A later milking time is another possible cause.
why.uz: Yozda faqat quruq pichan yegan sigir suti qishki sutday boʻlgan boʻlsa, farqni yangi oʻt beradi. Kech sogʻish boshqa ehtimoliy sabab.
why.ru: Если летом на одном сене молоко стало как зимнее, разницу даёт свежая трава. Поздняя дойка — другая возможная причина.

In a short story about a family trip, the narrator's father is described as someone who always plans for the worst, so that nothing can take him by surprise.

Which quotation from the story most effectively illustrates this description?

"He sang loudly with the radio for the whole of the drive, even the songs whose words he did not know at all."
"He had left the map at home, so we stopped twice to ask the way."
"He let my sister choose where we would stop for lunch."

why.en: Planning for the worst: three spare tires, a tent 'in case we got stranded' and a week of bread for a two-hour drive. Leaving the map at home shows the opposite.
why.uz: Eng yomoniga tayyorgarlik: uchta zaxira shina, chodir va ikki soatlik yoʻlga bir haftalik non. Xaritani uyda qoldirish buning teskarisi.
why.ru: Готовность к худшему: три запасных колеса, палатка на случай, если застрянут, и хлеб на неделю ради двух часов пути. Забытая карта — противоположность.

stem.en:
Bekzod hypothesized that playing music to the tomato plants in his family's greenhouse makes them grow faster. He played music in the greenhouse every day for a month, and the plants grew faster than they had the month before.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Bekzod's hypothesis?

The plants that grew fastest in Bekzod's greenhouse that month were the ones that stood closest to the speaker playing music.
Bekzod played the same music each day, always in the early morning.
Bekzod's family has grown tomatoes in the greenhouse for many years.

why.en: If plants with no music grew just as much faster in a warmer month, the warmth, not the music, explains it. Faster growth near the speaker would support him.

why.ru: Если томаты без музыки в более тёплый месяц тоже ускорили рост настолько же, дело в тепле, а не в музыке. Быстрый рост у динамика его бы поддержал.

A student writing about a poem claims that its speaker, remembering the summers she spent in her grandmother's garden, thinks of the garden as both a place of hard work and a place of rest.

Which quotation from the poem most effectively illustrates the student's claim?

options.en: "All morning we carried water to the rows, / and at noon we slept in the shade of the vine."
"All morning we carried water to the rows, / and pulled the weeds until our backs were sore."
"At noon we slept in the shade of the vine, / and the bees hummed in the quince tree above us."
"The garden gate was painted blue each spring, / the color of the sky above the hills."

why.en: Hard work: 'we carried water to the rows'. Rest: 'we slept in the shade of the vine'. Only this quotation has both; the others show one side or neither.
why.uz: Mehnat: «we carried water to the rows». Dam olish: «we slept in the shade of the vine». Ikkalasi faqat shu iqtibosda, boshqalarida bittasi yoki hech biri.
why.ru: Труд: «we carried water to the rows». Отдых: «we slept in the shade of the vine». Оба есть только в этой цитате; в других — одно из двух или ничего.

The town put up new traffic lights on Ulugbek's street and, in the same week, added three speed bumps. Since then, cars on the street have driven much more slowly. Ulugbek claims that the speed bumps, not the traffic lights, are what slowed the cars.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ulugbek's claim?

Cars on Ulugbek's street now drive much more slowly than they did before the changes.
On a nearby street that got speed bumps but no new lights, cars drove as fast as before.
Many drivers in the town say that they dislike driving over the speed bumps.

why.en: The claim credits the bumps, not the lights. A street with the lights alone and no slowdown rules out the lights. The slowdown on his street fits both causes.

A town found that its streets with the most trees have the fewest reports of broken windows. A council member concluded that planting trees makes people less likely to break windows.

In a short story, a student claims that the narrator's brother pretends not to care about the family's new puppy while secretly looking after it.

Which quotation from the story most effectively illustrates the student's claim?

options.en: "He said the puppy was a nuisance, but every night I heard him creep downstairs to check that its water bowl was full."
"He said the puppy was a nuisance and asked our parents to keep it out of his room."
"Every morning he filled its water bowl and took it for a walk around the yard before breakfast."

why.en: Pretends not to care: he calls it 'a nuisance'. Secretly cares: he creeps downstairs at night to check its water. Only this quotation shows both.

why.ru: Делает вид, что ему всё равно: называет щенка «a nuisance». Тайно заботится: ночью крадётся проверить воду. Обе стороны — только в этой цитате.

stem.en:
Abdulla's apple harvest was much smaller this year than last. In April there was a late frost, and two years ago he had replaced one corner of his orchard with a new variety of apple tree. Abdulla claims that the frost, not the new variety, caused the drop in his harvest.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Abdulla's claim?

options.en: The old trees in the orchard lost as large a share of their apples as the new trees did.
The new trees gave far fewer apples this year than the old trees did.
The new variety ripens about two weeks later than his old trees.
Several of Abdulla's neighbors planted the same new variety last year.

why.en: If the unchanged old trees lost as large a share as the new ones, the new variety cannot explain the drop, which fits the frost. Fewer apples on new trees would point to them.

A student claims that the greenhouse was at least 9 degrees warmer than the outside air at every time shown.

At 12:00 the greenhouse reached 26 °C, its highest temperature of the day.
The greenhouse was 9, 11, 11 and 8 degrees warmer at the four times shown.
Both temperatures were lowest at 8:00 and highest at 12:00.

why.en: 'At every time shown' needs all four gaps: 14 − 5 = 9, 26 − 15 = 11, 24 − 13 = 11 and 17 − 8 = 9, each at least 9 degrees.

A teacher claims that, from 2024 to 2025, buying lunch at the canteen went from being the less common choice to the more common one.

In both years, more of the school's students bought lunch at the canteen than brought it from home.

the van's journey was too rough for any kind of package.
biscuits sent in cardboard boxes will always arrive broken.
the biscuits packed in boxes had been baked for longer.

made that group work for more hours.
had little to do with how much was collected.
would double the litter collected on any river.

The difference in the bunches most likely comes from ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: cutting back the vines each winter.
the age of each family's vines.
the wooden frames the vines grow on.
the street where the families live.

why.en: Frames, kind of vine, planting year and street were the same and explain nothing; only the winter cutting differed, so the bigger bunches likely come from it.

let more road noise into the classroom.
made the traffic on the road less heavy.
made the meter in that room less accurate.

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: the sprints and jumps may have protected them better than stretching.
the coach's own way of training them caused most of the muscle injuries.
stretching before a match causes injuries in every sport.
both routines protected the players equally well.

why.en: Coach, pitch and league were shared and explain nothing; only the warm-up differed, and team B had far fewer injuries. One club's season says nothing of every sport.

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: showing drivers their own speed may slow them more than a fixed sign does.
the traffic outside School 9 was much lighter than at School 4.
fixed signs never have any effect on how fast anyone drives.
the speed limit near School 9 was lower than near School 4.

why.en: Limit and traffic were alike and explain nothing; only the kind of sign differed, and cars slowed at the flashing one. One month on two roads cannot show "never".

Anvar can most reasonably conclude that, in this orchard that year, the spring feeding ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: did little to make the hives stronger.
made the fed hives produce much more honey.
would make no difference in any orchard in any year.
harmed the bees in the hives that were fed.

why.en: Orchard and bees were the same; only the feeding differed, and bee numbers and honey were about equal, so it did little here. It says nothing about every year.

The results suggest that the short signs ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

helped visitors remember far more facts about the birds.
made visitors walk past the cages more quickly.
were less interesting to visitors than the long signs.

made the water in the covered wells colder.
had no effect on how clear the water stayed.
would keep any well clear in any kind of storm.

why.en: Depth and ground were the same; only the covers differed, and only the open wells turned cloudy after the dust storms, so the covers likely kept the dust out.

drew more visitors to the north pool at weekends as well.
made the south pool lose many of its usual visitors.
were the reason both pools were busier last summer.

made Hamida's shop sell more tea in all than Rahima's.
has no effect on which teas customers choose.
would make customers in any shop buy only costly tea.

made the plants grow taller in the end.
would make the seeds of every plant sprout sooner.
had no effect on when the seeds sprouted.

why.en: Kind, pots, shelf and watering were the same; only soaking differed, and the soaked seeds sprouted two days sooner. Nothing is said of later height or other plants.

was caused by how cold the winter was.
comes from the age of the two buildings.
shows that a meter cuts the heat any home uses by a quarter.

the flour used in that pie.
the heat of the oven that day.
the sugar added to that pie.

did not have his student card with him.
borrowed the laptop without asking anyone.
had lost his student card the week before.

put through Murod's own door.
kept at the post office.
lost in the flooded path.

the gas was on as usual.
the baker had run out of meat for the filling.
the bakery would bake no samsa the next day either.

why.en: Samsa is baked 'unless' the gas is cut, and the gas is cut 'only when' the pipes are repaired; no samsa was baked, so the gas was cut and the pipes were being repaired.
